why: Number of people who can use the facilities. I limited the range to 0-1,500 people/km2 to leave out towns: 1,102 on-grid facilities are in denser cells but only 26 unelectrified ones. With the default range Kampala comes 2nd even though it has no unelectrified facility.
Proxy for poverty. In the ANI poorer areas score higher, because facilities there are the least able to pay for electricity themselves.
The main layer for a health programme, so it gets the highest weight. 0-5 km keeps the analysis to areas within Uganda's 5 km access standard for health facilities.

Distance to the 11/33 kV grid. In the ANI areas further from the grid score higher. I did not use the >2 km filter from the lecture example because 68% of unelectrified facilities are within 1 km of a line.
